# dsh-restart

Restart DeepSeek Harness from the interface or with an agent tool — with the option to
continue the
same session after the start.
## What it does
| Capability | Where |

| "Restart" button | sidebar footer, next to the account (power icon) |
| Confirmation | a modal wit

h two buttons, no extra options |
| Agent tool | `dsh_restart({ fake, reason, plugins })` — for exte

nsion development only |
| Session continuation | a restart via the tool opens the session and write

s `[auto.continue.<token>]` |
| Watchdog window | while a restart runs: phase, timer, reason, plugin

s, live log tail |
| Recovery | rollback of the profile, quarantine of the suspect plugin, safe mode

live log tail |
| Recovery | rollback of the profile, quarantine of the suspect plugin, safe mode |
## How the restart works

The restarting process cannot be a child of the application: `taskkill /T` kills the whole
tree toge
ther with it. So the plugin:

1. writes the marker `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-restart\pending.json`;
2. stages the profile files that a r

estore may need (`prestart.json`, `pending-profile`);
3. creates a one-shot scheduler task `DSH-Rest

ow, closes the application's process tree, applies the
staged profile files while the app is down, l
aunches it again and deletes the task.

A boot counts as healthy only when the renderer reported in (`client-ready.json`) and no new
crash l

og appeared. Then the helper marks the current profile as the rollback target. When the
boot is not

healthy it restores `backup\last-good`, quarantines the plugins whose working tree
changed (their ed

its go to `git stash`), and starts again; if that still fails, it boots with
the base bundles only a
nd records safe mode in `safe-mode.json`.

The profile is never edited under a running app: `POST /profile/restore` stages the files and
the he

lper moves them into place while the app is down. Editing `package.json` or
`cordis.patch.yml` live
makes the loader re-apply the plugin tree and freezes the window.
## Auto-continue
After the start the client reads the marker through the local bridge `127.0.0.1:49233`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The continuation text carries the restart token: `[auto.continue.<token>]`, or
`[auto.continue.faile

d.<token>]` after an unrecovered boot. The token is the same one in
`pending.json` and `overlay.json

`, so a duplicated or lost message in the chat can be traced to
its restart. A marker is delivered t

o one client only — a 15 second lock plus a persistent
`deliveredAt` field — and a single attempt se

nds at most once: the client clicks the send
button, waits for the composer to clear, and never mixe
s the button with Enter.

A restart via the tool returns the session with that message: the client opens the same
session, wai

ts for the composer to be ready, inserts the text and sends it. The sidebar footer
button does not c
reate a marker and does not continue the session.

The user's draft is not lost: if the field already contains text, it is temporarily stashed
in `loca

lStorage`, the marker is sent, and then the text is returned to the input field
(without being sent)

. The message queue is session state — the plugin neither reads nor
changes it.
## The tool

The tool exists for developing and debugging DSH itself: a plugin, `cordis.patch.yml`, the
profile.

It is not intended for ordinary work, for "refreshing state", or for calls without
a code/config cha
nge that needs a fresh process.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Without `fake` the tool restarts the application and returns the session with an
`[auto.continue]` m

essage. The `fake` flag runs every check but restarts nothing — for
tests. If the tool is disabled,

a call from old memory fails with
`unknown tool "dsh_restart"`.
## Plugin settings
On the Plugins → Restart → Configure page:
| Setting | Default | What it does |
| Language | Russian | language of the button and the form: Russian, English, Chinese, or "Auto" (fo

llows the application language) |
| The `dsh_restart` command is available to the agent | enabled |
when disabled the tool disappears; a call from old memory fails with `unknown tool "dsh_restart"` |
| Watchdog active | enabled | when disabled a restart just closes and opens the application, with no

profile rollback |
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- a **tray** item and an entry in the native **Application** menu cannot be added by the
plugin: the

tray and the menu live in the Electron main process, while the plugin lives
in a child host process

he restart will not work;
- workspace sessions that are executing a turn at that moment will be inte

th tkinter and a graphical session; without them the
PowerShell window (Windows) or a console tail i

ter and a graphical session; without them the
PowerShell window (Windows) or a console tail is used.
### Known limitation: a subagent's job after its completion

If a subagent started a background job and finished its turn, DSH deletes the record of
that job tog

ether with the agent, although the job itself keeps running. The pre-restart
check **will not see**
such a job and will not refuse the restart.
What is covered:
| Owner of the work | Refusal |

| Own background job | yes |
| A subagent or another session is still working | yes |
| Their jobs,

while the owner is alive | yes |
| A subagent's job after its turn finished | no |

Why: the job registry `ctx.jobs` is keyed by agent id and is cleared when the agent is
destroyed; th

e `jobs.start` wrapper sees only jobs started through that path, while a
subagent starts them differ

ently. Detection by child processes is unreliable: the
application's service processes constantly ap

pear and disappear nearby. The solution is
deferred.
